Fr8Labs Design System

Build freight workflows from shared decisions.

FDS gives designers and engineers one documented foundation for accessible controls, consistent interaction rules, and reusable freight-workflow patterns.

01 · Install

Start with the complete FDS surface

Install components, icons, and tokens together in a supported React 19 and Vite browser application.

Open the installation guide →

Current release: components and tokens v0.3.0 · icons v0.1.1

02 · Browse

Move from foundations to finished workflows

Use the catalog to find the smallest established decision. Start with components, then use foundations or approved patterns when needed.

Component library→

Actions, inputs, feedback, data display, navigation, layout, and overlays

 Foundations→

Design principles, tokens, icon names, visual roles, and implementation vocabulary

 Workflow patterns→

Approved compositions using synthetic freight data

03 · Understand

Adopt from the workflow outward

FDS is a working method as much as a component library. Begin with the freight task and finish by validating the assembled workflow in product.

  1. 01Define the workflow

    Name the task, user role, real content, and required states.

  2. 02Assemble approved parts

    Reuse documented tokens, components, and patterns before adding a new decision.

  3. 03Validate in product

    Test responsive layout, keyboard paths, accessible names, and workflow meaning.

Current release · components/tokens v0.3.0 · icons v0.1.1

Changelog

See what changed in each package version.

19–21 Aug 2026

Components/tokens 0.3.0 · icons 0.1.1

Breaking changes

  • Removed duplicate CSS token aliases. Replace aliases such as --spacing-3 with their --fds-* semantic equivalent.

Changed

  • Updated component styles to use canonical FDS tokens only.
  • Refined the Token Foundation documentation and added the Design Principles reference for operational workflows.
  • Kept sandbox-fds-icons at 0.1.1 because its package implementation did not change.

18 Aug 2026

Components/tokens 0.2.0 · icons 0.1.1

Breaking changes

  • InlineAlert is dismissible by default. Set persistent when the message must remain until its workflow state is resolved.
  • Existing neutral, feedback, shadow, and Button token values changed. Consumers that copied raw values should migrate to the published semantic or component tokens.

Added

  • Added the floating Notification component with optional title, lists, embedded links, one action, and dismissal.
  • Added InlineAlert size, emphasis, list, persistence, and dismissal APIs.
  • Added exported breakpoint data and semantic form, reading, and page-width tokens.

Changed

  • Refined Button structure, status colors, alert contrast, overlay shadows, and compact responsive behavior.
  • Expanded the icon catalog and refreshed Getting Started, component, icon, and token documentation.
  • Kept sandbox-fds-icons at 0.1.1 because its package implementation did not change.

18 Aug 2026

0.1.2

Fixed

  • Corrected the npm installation and setup documentation.
  • Removed internal catalog content from the npm package artifact.
  • Added explicit testing-release and repository metadata.

2026-07-14

0.1.1

Added

  • First approved pilot release of the sandbox-fds-components package.

For compatibility and setup, use the FDS installation guide.

Versioning policy

Each package follows Semantic Versioning. While the major version is 0, its public contract may change between minor releases, so review every changelog entry before upgrading.

The canonical component release history is packages/components/CHANGELOG.md. Keep this page aligned with all three package manifests and the approved catalog whenever a package version changes.

import {Meta, Source} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import './Welcome.css';

Getting started · Read-only public pilot

MCP pilot

Test whether an AI assistant can find and apply approved FDS guidance through read-only catalog access.

Access
Published FDS catalog and Storybook documentation
Permissions
Read-only
Data
Synthetic data only

Connect

Use the shared pilot

Connect to the hosted endpoint to test the published FDS catalog and Storybook documentation. No repository clone or local server is required. The endpoint exposes guidance only; it does not install FDS or edit the application.

Local validation

Run current source before deployment

Start the local server when validating source changes, then connect the client to http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp.

Configure

Add FDS to the MCP client

Add the server, then restart the client. Use the local URL instead when testing source changes; both endpoints expose the same nine read-only tools.

Reference

Available tools

Use catalog tools to find approved FDS records and documentation tools to retrieve published guidance and examples.

search_catalog
Find approved records by query, kind, or FDS version.
get_component
Return an approved component API, dependencies, states, accessibility constraints, and code snapshot.
get_template
Return an approved fake-data template, allowed composition, accessibility constraints, and code snapshot.
get_prompt
Return an approved bounded prompt and its fake-data restriction without running it.
get_token_reference
Resolve an approved token to its CSS variable, alias, and permitted use.
get_adoption_recipe
Return versioned package or owned-copy instructions and the related drift warning.
list-all-documentation
List the IDs for every published Storybook component, pattern, foundation, document, and story.
get-documentation
Return the API, props, guidance, and example stories for one Storybook entry.
get-documentation-for-story
Return the usage example for one published story scenario.

Validate

Run the pilot

Follow the prompts in order so the assistant discovers the documentation before it applies component guidance.

  1. Ask: “List all FDS Storybook documentation and include story IDs.”

  2. Ask: “Get the documentation for components-actions-button and use its real props and examples.”

  3. Ask: “Get the approved Button catalog record and package adoption recipe.”

  4. Confirm the recipe matches the FDS installation guide.

  5. Use the returned guidance in a disposable Vite application and verify that the sample compiles and renders.

Keep pilot data synthetic

Do not send customer, shipment, invoice, credential, or production data through the pilot.

Finish

Report the result

Record anything that was missing, confusing, or incorrect so the catalog and documentation can be improved.

  • MCP client
  • Prompts used
  • Returned FDS version and item IDs
  • Final outcome

Fr8Labs Design System

Contributing

Keep reusable decisions in FDS and feature-specific work in the product that owns the workflow.

Choose the right home

  • Reuse an existing component or pattern before adding another one.
  • Put reusable components, tokens, and interaction rules in FDS.
  • Put feature-specific concrete prototypes in the prototyping project.
  • Treat sandbox work as exploration until it is explicitly approved.

Use the Storybook hierarchy

  • Components/<Category>/<Component>
  • Patterns/<Workflow category>/<Pattern>
  • Foundations/<Foundation>
  • Internal/<Purpose>/<Check>

Name story exports after the scenario, state, or decision they demonstrate.

Verify before review

Passing checks confirms implementation quality; reusable design still requires explicit review and approval.

foundations-design-principles--docs.content:
import {Meta} from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'; import './DesignPrinciples.css';

Foundations · Approved FDS v1

Design principles for operational work

The shared decision framework for freight workflows: clear status, confident review, fast repeated work, and accessible detail.

10 principles
One framework for FDS decisions
Freight workflows
Operations, accounting, documents, and approvals
Evidence before variation
Reuse an approved decision first

Check every design against these ten principles

Use each statement as a test for a proposed workflow, component, token, or pattern.

  1. 01

    Dense but legible

    Show enough operational detail to support a decision without crowding controls or text.

  2. 02

    Status first

    State the current shipment, invoice, document, approval, or exception status in text—not color alone.

  3. 03

    Audit-friendly

    Keep identifiers, owners, timestamps, and state changes beside the decision they explain.

  4. 04

    Fast repeated work

    Make recurring review fast with keyboard paths, predictable filters, and compact controls.

  5. 05

    Plain business language

    Use one consistent freight term for each concept, including shipment job, HBL, MBL, invoice, charge, AR, AP, and approval.

  6. 06

    Accessible by default

    Provide persistent labels, visible focus, sufficient contrast, keyboard paths, readable text, and accessible names.

  7. 07

    Component decisions serve workflows

    Choose components for the shipment, accounting, document, or approval task they clarify—not because they look modern.

  8. 08

    Reference, do not copy

    Use legacy screens and Figma files to understand business behaviour, not to define the FDS visual foundation.

  9. 09

    Stable Fr8Labs contracts

    Build with published FDS components, icons, and tokens—not the internal primitives behind them.

  10. 10

    Reuse before variation

    Start with an approved component or composition. Create an exception only when workflow evidence justifies it.

Release review for FDS changes

For designers and engineers contributing to FDS. Product teams using approved FDS components can skip this workflow.

  1. 01

    Contributor

    Document principle fit

    In the proposal, name each principle the change supports.

  2. 02

    Maintainer

    Resolve conflicts before release

    Confirm that every conflict has a principle amendment or an approved exception.
